analysis:
Both units are base-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 718-1238). The patch for this file changes only documentation: the heading goes from 'v0.10.3 candidate' to 'v0.10.4 candidate', and upgrade and rollout notes are added (head lines 11-171). No executable code, configuration, workflow or threat-model definitions are modified in the supplied evidence. The base text is historical release notes and was not re-reviewed as new behavior.

Security-relevant claims in the changelog text, which this pass cannot verify against source:
- T-041/SEC-035 (cache): SSD cache write budget raised to 4 TB/day; deeper SSD restores on large-memory Macs; segment retention. These are described as operational tuning. The 30-minute TTL, the HMAC lookup tags and the account-scoped cacheSalt are not stated to change. Any real code change to these would need a SEC-035 sign-off, and that code was not supplied.
- Staging release lane and an installer signature relaxation for '-dev.' and '-staging.' versions (scripts/install.sh, release workflows). The notes say production keeps the full Apple-team requirement, and that prod is tag-gated and never receives PROD_* secrets from master pushes. These are release-pipeline and installer controls that the supplied excerpts do not show. A reviewer of the actual script and workflow diffs should confirm that the relaxation cannot be triggered for production bundles through version-string spoofing. This is a question for integration, not a finding.
- Coordinator/provider rollout coupling (prompt_anchor_mismatch quarantining cache affinity for up to 10 minutes on version skew) is an availability and routing note outside this repo. Platform-owned.

No regression is evidenced from the changelog alone. The head-side text is truncated, so code changes behind these entries must be reviewed in their own units.
